Bleckmann Lutterworth Distribution Centre Goes Live

# Latest Bleckmann DC in Lutterworth celebrates going live

 23 July 2026 

Bleckmann, a specialist in supply chain management for fashion and lifestyle brands, is celebrating the go-live of its latest mega distribution centre (DC) in Lutterworth. In less than four months, the new warehouse has been fully prepared for operations. This clearly demonstrates Bleckmann’s speed and flexibility, which enable the company to scale up. 

The warehouse, located in the Midlands’ ‘Golden Triangle’, is suitable for categories such as beauty, hair care, sports and accessories, as well as fashion clothing.

The opening of the DC, which covers 761,932 square feet (70,786 square metres), marks a significant milestone for Bleckmann in the further expansion of its lifestyle logistics offering. With the successful go-live, a key milestone has been reached, and the company is ready to operate at full capacity.

#### CEVA Logistics opens new distribution facility in Derby to support eCommerce growth 

- Date : July 18 2026, 7:16 pm 
- Author : Logistics Monitor 

CEVA Logistics, a global leader in third-party logistics, has announced the opening of a new large-scale warehouse operation in Derby, UK, marking another significant milestone for the company and further strengthening its position as a strategic logistics partner for leading global eCommerce brands.

The new operation, scheduled to go live in August 2026, will see CEVA manage a dedicated facility designed to support the rapid deployment of fast-moving inventory for fulfilment to end-customers across the UK.

Supporting regional eCommerce Growth 

CEVA will operate the new 508,000-square-foot warehouse facility in Derby to manage the storage, handling and distribution of customer inventory, enabling faster, more efficient customer deliveries across the UK. # Translink Express makes four senior appointments

Leicestershire logistics firm Translink Express Logistics has made four senior appointments following 32 per cent growth over the past two years.

Lee Barrett has been promoted to head of traffic; Dan Green takes the newly created role of head of project management; and Shanice Walsh becomes head of operations.

Ryan Wallis has also joined the family-owned business as head of warehousing.

The new management team will take responsibility for the day-to-day running of Translink Express, allowing its directors to focus more closely on long-term strategy as the business approaches its 40th anniversary.

Chris Hobbis, director at Translink Express Logistics, said: “In two years we’ve seen record growth – just shy of 32 per cent, which is phenomenal.

# Automation with a purpose: why sustainability must be at the heart of the modern warehouse

Posted on Tuesday 1 September 2026 Share: 

The warehouse has undergone a remarkable transformation over the last decade, says Yusen Logistics UK.

ONCE VIEWED primarily as a storage location within the supply chain, today’s warehouse has become a critical hub for operational excellence, customer experience, business resilience and sustainability. As supply chains become increasingly complex, organisations are under growing pressure to deliver greater speed, accuracy and flexibility while reducing environmental impact and controlling costs.

For many businesses, warehouse automation has become a key part of the solution. However, automation alone is no longer enough.

# Major changes at fast-growing Leicestershire logistics firm

27 Aug 26

Translink Express Logistics announces four senior leadership appointments and plans to transform 66,000 sq. ft premises into huge pallet sortation centre

Translink Express Logistics announces four senior leadership appointments and plans to transform 66,000 sq. ft premises into huge pallet sortation centre

A Leicestershire logistics firm which has grown by a record 32 per cent over the last two years has made four senior leadership appointments as it approaches its 40th anniversary.

Translink Express Logistics has promoted three members of its team to senior roles, with Lee Barrett becoming Head of Traffic; Dan Green taking up a newly created position of Head of Project Management and Shanice Walsh promoted to Head of Operations.

The fourth appointment is a new hire, with Ryan Wallis joining the firm as Head of Warehousing.
